description: Working-tree and ignore-rule hygiene: finalize .gitignore and remove dead/vestigial and regenerable files so the repo is clean to push. Scoped strictly to the quantum_traffic_optimizer folder. Independent of FEAT-001 (touches different files) but ordered after it so the final git commit (done in the merge/finalize step) sees both the doc fixes and the tidy tree.
steps: Edit .gitignore: append 'redlight_violations/' and '*.mp4' (loose test videos) to the Generated-data section. Keep all existing rules (.env, __pycache__/, *.pyc, .venv/, venv/, wheels/, *.engine, accident_snapshots/, speed_violations/, traffic_log.json, traffic_logs.csv). Keep .env ignored; do NOT ignore .env.example.
Delete the empty unused directory pages/ (Remove-Item -Recurse -Force pages).
Delete redlight_violations/ from the working tree (old Jetson-project output; grep 'redlight' across repo .py files returns zero matches, nothing writes it).

Delete the regenerable runtime artifacts from the working tree: traffic_log.json, traffic_logs.csv, and the contents/dirs accident_snapshots/ and speed_violations/. They stay gitignored and are recreated at runtime by logger.py / video_detector.py.

Do NOT delete .env from disk. Do NOT delete yolo11s.pt or accident_ncnn_model/ (model weights, each < 50MB, keep). Do NOT delete wheels/ (gitignored, leave on disk). Do NOT touch anything outside the quantum_traffic_optimizer folder, especially the sibling '..\Jetson Orin Traffic System Backup\' folder and parent-level *.mp4 files.
acceptance_criteria: Test-Path for pages, redlight_violations, traffic_log.json, traffic_logs.csv all return False.
Test-Path for yolo11s.pt, accident_ncnn_model\model.ncnn.bin, .env, .env.example all return True.
git check-ignore redlight_violations/ and git check-ignore .env both report the path as ignored.
git check-ignore .env.example reports nothing (it is NOT ignored).
All 18 (or remaining) .py modules still pass python -m py_compile after cleanup.
verification: PowerShell: git check-ignore redlight_violations/ ; git check-ignore .env ; git check-ignore .env.example  (first two print the path, last prints nothing)

python -c "from traffic_network import TrafficNetwork; from quantum_optimizer import optimize_signals, apply_assignment; from classical_baseline import solve_fixed; from environmental import evaluate_plan, improvement; net=TrafficNetwork(6,7); net.randomize_traffic(0.5); r=optimize_signals(net); apply_assignment(net,r); print('run OK', r.method)"
findings: .gitignore finalized: appended 'redlight_violations/' to Generated-data section and added a '# Loose test videos' section with '*.mp4'; all prior rules kept (.env ignored, .env.example NOT ignored). Deleted from working tree: pages/, redlight_violations/, accident_snapshots/, speed_violations/, traffic_log.json, traffic_logs.csv. Kept on disk as required: .env, .env.example, yolo11s.pt, accident_ncnn_model/, wheels/. Verification all passed: Test-Path pages/redlight_violations/traffic_log.json/traffic_logs.csv = False; yolo11s.pt/accident_ncnn_model\model.ncnn.bin/.env/.env.example = True; git check-ignore reports redlight_violations/ and .env ignored, .env.example not ignored; all .py modules py_compile clean; app-logic chain prints 'run OK Simulated Annealing (classical fallback)'. Committed locally on branch main; .env confirmed NOT staged. Note: __pycache__/ regenerated by py_compile is gitignored (untracked, not committed).
